title: Mixed practice: Why early cities grew beside rivers
description: One set with every response type: reading, listening, speaking and writing about early river civilizations.

stimuli.title: Why Early Cities Grew Beside Rivers
paragraphs: Some of the first cities in history developed near rivers. In Mesopotamia, the land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, and in Egypt, along the Nile, farming communities grew into large cities more than five thousand years ago. These places share an important feature: a dependable supply of fresh water.

Rivers supported agriculture in several ways. Each year, the Nile flooded and left behind a layer of rich silt, which made the soil fertile. In Mesopotamia, where rain was unpredictable, farmers dug canals to carry river water to their fields. As a result, they could grow more food than their families needed.

A surplus of food changed society. Because fewer people had to farm, some could become builders, potters, priests, or traders. Cities needed leaders to organize canal building and to store the extra grain, so governments also began to develop.

Rivers also served as roads. Boats carried grain, pottery, and stone between towns much faster than people could carry loads over land. Trade spread new ideas as well as goods. Although rivers brought floods that could destroy homes, the benefits of water, food, and transportation outweighed the risks for most communities.

stimuli.title: Listen: A lab safety briefing
stimuli.script: Teacher: Before we begin the filtering experiment, I want to explain two rules. Student one: Do we need goggles? Teacher: Yes, goggles are required the whole time, even if you are only watching. Student two: What about the dirty water? Teacher: Never drink it, and never pour it down the sink. Pour it into the blue container on the side table. Student one: And if we spill? Teacher: Stop, step back, and tell me right away. Do not wipe it up yourself.

stimuli.title: Speaking task
paragraphs: A river city sells grain in baskets. Basket A holds 12 kilograms and costs 30 coins. Basket B holds 20 kilograms and costs 45 coins. Explain which basket is the better buy and justify your answer with numbers.

stimuli.title: Writing task
paragraphs: Do you agree that rivers were the most important reason early cities grew? Write a claim. Support it with at least two reasons from the passage “Why Early Cities Grew Beside Rivers.”

stimuli.title: Data: Three river cities
stimuli.caption: Three early river cities and one resource each used.

items.stem: According to paragraph 3, why did governments begin to develop?

options.text: People wanted to fight wars over the rivers.
Priests and potters asked for taxes.
Cities needed leaders to organize canal building and store extra grain.
Traders needed to build roads on land.

distractors.a: The passage does not mention wars.
distractors.b: Priests and potters are listed as jobs, not as the reason for governments.
distractors.d: Paragraph 4 says boats, not land roads, moved goods.

items.explanation: Paragraph 3 says cities needed leaders to organize canal building and to store extra grain.

support.clue: Reread paragraph 3. Look for the word “so” near the end: it connects a need to a result.
support.frame: Governments developed because cities needed ______ to ______.
support.model: Mentor example (different topic). “The school needed a schedule so the buses could arrive on time, so a transportation office was created.” The need leads to the new office.

items.stem: Which two details show how rivers helped farming?

options.text: The Nile flood left rich silt on the land.
Farmers in Mesopotamia dug canals to carry water.

distractors.b: This shows how rivers helped trade, not farming.
distractors.d: This is a result of farming, not a way the river helped it.

items.explanation: Silt made the soil fertile and canals moved water to the fields: both are about farming.

support.clue: Reread paragraph 2 only. The question asks about farming, not trade.
support.frame: Rivers helped farming because ______ and because ______.
support.model: Mentor example. “A well helped the village’s gardens in two ways: it supplied water, and it let families plant in dry months.” Find two ways in your paragraph.

items.stem: Choose the best connecting words to complete the argument.

dropdown.template: Rivers brought floods; {1}, most communities stayed because rivers gave them water and food. {2} farmers could grow more food than they needed, some people could do other jobs.

items.explanation: “However” signals a contrast with the floods; “Because” gives the reason that some people could do other jobs.

support.clue: Decide for each blank: is the second idea a contrast, a reason, or an example of the first?
support.frame: The first idea is bad, ______ the second idea is good. / ______ this happened, that happened.
support.model: Mentor example. “The bus was late; however, we still arrived on time. Because the road was clear, the driver went fast.” Notice contrast versus reason.

items.stem: Put the cause-and-effect chain in order.

items.text: Fewer people had to farm, so some became builders, potters, or traders.
Rivers gave farmers water and fertile soil.
Cities needed leaders, so governments developed.
Farmers grew a surplus of food.

items.explanation: Water and soil led to surplus food, then new jobs, then governments.

support.clue: Find the first cause in paragraph 2, and follow the words “As a result,” “Because,” and “so.”
support.frame: First, ______. As a result, ______. Because of this, ______. So ______.
support.model: Mentor example. “It rained a lot, so the river rose. Because the river rose, the road flooded. As a result, school closed.” Each result becomes the next cause.

items.stem: Use the table. Match each city to the resource it used.
items.explanation: Read across each row of the table.

support.clue: Put one finger on a city in the first column, then slide across the row to the third column.
support.model: Mentor example table: Maya | corn | food. Read it as “Maya used corn for food.”

items.stem: Sort each statement: is it a benefit of rivers or a risk?

tokens.text: Boats move grain faster than people on land.

items.explanation: The passage names floods and unpredictable rain as risks, and silt and faster boat travel as benefits.

support.clue: Ask: does this help a community or hurt it? Find the word “risks” in paragraph 4.
support.frame: This is a benefit because it ______. This is a risk because it ______.
support.model: Mentor example. “A bridge shortens the trip (benefit), but it can break in a storm (risk).”

items.stem: What should students do if the dirty water spills?

options.text: Wipe it up with paper towels.
Pour the rest into the sink.
Stop, step back, and tell the teacher.

distractors.a: The teacher says not to wipe it up yourself.
distractors.b: The teacher says never to pour dirty water down the sink.
distractors.c: Goggles are required the whole time, but that is not the spill instruction.

items.explanation: The teacher says: stop, step back, and tell me right away. Do not wipe it up yourself.

support.clue: Listen for the last student question and the teacher’s answer. Listen for the word “spill.”
support.frame: If water spills, students should first ______ and then ______.
support.model: Mentor example. “If the alarm rings, stop working, line up quietly, and wait for me.” Notice the order of actions.

items.stem: Write a claim about rivers and early cities. Support it with two reasons from the passage.

checklist: I gave two reasons from the passage.
I used a connecting word such as because, however, or as a result.
I explained how each reason supports my claim.

support.clue: List two benefits of rivers from the passage. Which one does the most to explain why cities grew?
support.frame: I agree that ______ because ______. In addition, ______. This shows that ______.
support.model:
Mentor example about a different claim. “I think the library is the best place in school because it is quiet. In addition, it has books for every interest. This shows that students can learn well there.” Notice the claim first, then two reasons, then what they show.

Write about rivers the same way.

items.stem: Explain which basket is the better buy and justify your answer.

checklist: I compared the two baskets with numbers.
I stated which basket is the better buy.
I used a reason word such as because or since.

support.clue: Find the price for one kilogram of each basket. Think: coins divided by kilograms.
support.frame: Basket A costs ______ coins for each kilogram. Basket B costs ______. So basket ___ is the better buy because ______.
support.model: Mentor example with different numbers. “Bag X is 8 coins for 4 kilograms, which is 2 coins each. Bag Y is 9 coins for 3 kilograms, which is 3 coins each. So bag X is the better buy because it costs less for each kilogram.”
